intended_object: The diagonal group scheme D_n over Spec K, together with its n coordinate projections D_n → G_m to the multiplicative group, viewed as a fan (a cone over the discrete diagram j ↦ G_m) in the category of group objects over Spec K. This is the cone that exhibits D_n ≅ G_m^n (Milne, Algebraic Groups, §12.d). Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and how the library uses it in `diagonalGroupProductFan_isLimit`.
explanation:
I judge this definition faithful. It is `Limits.Fan.mk (diagonalGroupScheme K n) (diagonalGroupProjection K n)`. That is, the cone point is the diagonal group scheme, and the j-th leg is the morphism of group objects given by Spec of a Hopf-algebra map.

That Hopf-algebra map sends the Laurent coordinate t of G_m to the j-th diagonal entry x_jj of the coordinate ring of D_n. This is the standard j-th coordinate projection: on R-points it sends a diagonal matrix to its j-th invertible entry (`diagonalGroupProjection_point`). The library then proves that this fan is a limit, both after forgetting to schemes over Spec K and in group objects. This is the expected product structure D_n ≅ ∏ G_m.

On generality: the base is an arbitrary commutative ring K, and the index set is an arbitrary finite type with decidable equality, which is the natural setting. Finiteness is needed for D_n to be an affine group scheme of finite type. Mathlib has no diagonal group scheme or projection fan of this kind. Since this is a specific object, it is not too narrow.
